title: What The Erhu Knows (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word observational 100bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal Chinese philosophy absurdist
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The erhu is a two-string instrument from ancient China
Two strings should be enough for something fine
But between those two strings lives a universe of feeling
That makes every other instrument seem like it's still healing

[Pre-Chorus]
I asked a man to teach me one afternoon in Chinatown
He handed it to me and said "breathe" — I nearly put it down

[Chorus]
What does the erhu know that I don't know?
It's been carrying sorrow since the Tang dynasty's last show
What does the erhu know in the still of night?
It knows the sound of longing fits inside two strings held tight
That's my boy

[Verse 2]
The bow moves through the strings like wind through river reeds
It doesn't pluck or strum, it breathes and breathes and breathes
There's a courtyard in every note, a dynasty in every phrase
The erhu has been practicing for over a thousand days

[Bridge]
Some say it sounds like weeping, some say it sounds like joy
I say it sounds like both at once, which is the whole decoy
I cannot play the erhu but I understand its logic
One voice, two strings, the whole human condition — classic

[Outro]
Erhu knows… two strings, infinite feeling… erhu knows
That's my boy
